Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO weeks after his resignation
The ousted CEO has been reinstated by the board less than two weeks after his ouster, in consultation with senior officials from the United States government.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 23, 2026
schedule
1 Min Read
expand_content
Image via Nvidia
Nvidia has announced this morning that Jensen Huang,
the once-former Nvidia CEO and founder that resigned 11 days ago
after a number of extramarital affairs—including those that potentially affected national security and some subordinates—came to light, has been reinstated by the board as the president and CEO of the company.
The statement from Nvidia announcing this reversal
also states the decision was made in consultation with senior officials in the US government.
This unprecedented about-face for one of the largest companies in the world indicates a deep unease with the way Nvidia's stock price has been trending since Huang's departure. US president Donald Trump has also been beating the drum to reinstate Huang to the CEO position, though he has not made it clear why he believes Huang should return. In the end, the statement's consultation note could suggest that Trump’s camp made a convincing argument to Nvidia’s board of directors, who made a unanimous decision to reinstate Huang after previously stating that they will not bow to pressure to do so.
Related:
Grand Theft Auto VI is now the biggest video game launch in history
Due to Huang's previous involvement as the target of a foreign intelligence investigation, Nvidia is also putting together a committee to assist with the investigation, or whatever remains of the investigation. Nvidia has also put together a council to work with the government on national security matters.
Nvidia stock, meanwhile, is up 30 percent today.
